name: Seep
description: Seep is a four-player partnership fishing game played in the Punjab and other parts of India and Pakistan. Players capture cards from a layout; building piles called houses and scoring for sweeps. Related to Casino and Royal Casino.

overview.description: Seep is a four-player partnership fishing game played in the Punjab and other parts of India and Pakistan. Players capture cards from a layout; building piles called houses and scoring for sweeps. Related to Casino and Royal Casino.

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: India, Pakistan (Punjab).
Time Period: Traditional; 30-point version is possibly older and very popular in the Punjab.
Historical Development: Fishing game related to Casino and Royal Casino; northern India version has 100-point total; Punjab version 30 points.
Cultural Significance: Popular partnership game in Punjab (India and Pakistan).
timeline: Traditional: Played in Punjab (India and Pakistan); 30-point version possibly older
Modern Era: Popular in India, Pakistan; digital versions available

setup.players: Four players in fixed partnerships (partners opposite). Deal and play counter-clockwise. Two-player variant exists.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack, no jokers. English pattern.
setup.dealing: Dealer gives 4 cards to player on right and 4 face down on table. That player bids (9–13) and plays one card from the four; dealer then deals the rest in groups of four counter-clockwise. Bidder ends with 11 cards, others 12.
setup.equipment: Standard 52-card deck, score sheet (optional), table space.

rules.objective: Capture cards worth points from the layout (floor). The game ends when one team has a lead of at least 100 points over the other (a baazi). Capture by playing a card that matches the capture value of one or more cards or houses on the table; build houses (piles that can only be captured as a unit) to protect or consolidate captures.
rules.gameplay: Deal: First dealer random; dealer gives 4 cards to player on right and 4 face down on table. That player bids 9–13 (capture value) if possible, then must create a house of that value, pick up cards of that value, or throw the bid card as loose. Dealer then deals remainder in fours counter-clockwise (bidder has 11 cards, others 12). Play proceeds counter-clockwise. Each turn: play one card to (1) create or add to a house, (2) pick up matching cards or houses, or (3) throw a loose card. Houses are piles of 9–13 capture value; ordinary houses can be broken or cemented; cemented houses cannot be broken. Must pick up all cards that match the played card. Sweep (taking all floor cards) scores 50 (25 on first play, 0 on last). Last picker takes any remaining loose cards.
keyRules: Capture value: A=1, 2–10 face, J=11, Q=12, K=13
Only spades (1–13), aces of other suits (1 each), and 10♦ (6) score; total 100 points
First team to lead by 100 wins one baazi; team scoring under 9 in a deal loses a baazi immediately
House owner must hold a card matching house value until captured or broken

strategy.basic: Remember cards left in denominations 9–K and point-carrying cards picked up. Try to leave only two items on the floor when possible.
strategy.intermediate: Ensure your side is last to pick up so you take remaining loose cards at end. Cement houses you want to keep; pick up with point cards if you fear the house will be broken or taken.
strategy.advanced: If you and partner hold all four of a denomination, build a cemented house in that value; opponents cannot break or capture it. Use house ownership and card memory to force favourable end-game.
tips: Leave two items totalling at least 14 when possible to reduce sweep risk
Dealer can delay picking up a cemented house until last turn to keep loose cards for your team

variations.name: Two-Player Game
variations.description: Four hands dealt; two to players, two face down. Play 12 cards each; remaining loose cards stay. Each player picks up one face-down hand and play continues. Transition is vulnerable to sweeps.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation does not change engine constants; only table rules.

variations.name: Limited Houses
variations.description: Only two houses allowed on the floor at once. Creating a third is illegal; player must throw or pick up.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: No engine overrides; only house limit rule.

variations.name: Scoring variation
variations.description: 10♦ worth 2 instead of 6; 4 points for majority of cards (more than 26); total still 100. Some allow breaking a house with a floor card plus hand card to cement.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Scoring and optional break rule only; no engine keys.

variations.name: 30-point Seep
variations.description: Punjab version: 10♦=12, 9♠=9, 2♠=1, each ace=1; 4 for majority of cards (total 30). Sweep worth capture value of card played. Deal restarted if table has 10♦ or 9♠. Satthi (all 30 in one deal) = 60 points.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Different point total and deal check; no engine overrides.

scoring.description: Spades 1–13 points (K=13 down to A=1), aces of other suits 1 each, 10♦ = 6; total 100. Sweep: 50 (25 on first play, 0 on last). First team to lead by 100 wins one baazi. Team scoring under 9 in a deal loses a baazi.
scoring.winCondition: First team to achieve a lead of 100 or more points over the other team wins one baazi. Team scoring fewer than 9 points in a deal loses a baazi immediately.
